commit.message:
fix: capture each device's artefacts before the next build removes them

The previous commit was half a fix. It supplied the bootloader that stopped
being built, and the v1.12.15 run then failed one step earlier, writing it:

  FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory:
    '.pio/build/gh_release_x4pro/bootloader.bin'

Not the file this time. The DIRECTORY. After both builds, x4pro's output
directory does not exist, and the sticky build says so in passing:

  [ComponentManager] Updated build file (55 total removals)

So there were two faults stacked, and fixing the visible one exposed the
other. Naming both devices' artefacts at the end reads the second build's
leftovers for the first, and firmware.bin and partitions.bin were as exposed
as the bootloader; merge-bin just happened to name the bootloader first.

Each device is now built, given its bootloader, and named, before the next
build starts. That is robust without knowing exactly what ComponentManager
removes or why, which is the right shape of fix for a teardown nobody here
controls.

host-tests/release asserts the order that broke: the sticky build must not run
before the x4pro artefacts are named. Watched it fail with the old order put
back, naming both line numbers, and pass restored.

Board card #155.

commit.message:
fix: the release takes the bootloader from the framework package

v1.12.14 tagged and then could not publish. crossplay-release.yml failed at
merge-bin, deterministically, three runs including a rerun:

  [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.pio/build/gh_release_x4pro/bootloader.bin'

e31dcbb0 ("don't recompile Arduino IDF libs", upstream #3242) stopped
compiling the IDF, and that file was a by-product of the compile. The firmware
builds still pass without it, because only merge-bin ever reads it, so this
was invisible everywhere except the one job that publishes.

Ruled out first, each with evidence rather than reasoning: esptool (the
workflow upgrades it unpinned and got 5.4.0 where v1.12.13 used 5.1.2, but
5.4.0 runs that exact command correctly on dummy files here); the PlatformIO
cache (both runs logged "Cache not found"); the platform (pinned to 55.03.37
and identical in both); and patch_pioarduino_cache.py silently no-opping (it
raises when neither string matches, and the builds succeeded). The tell was in
the logs: the v1.12.13 run compiled dozens of bootloader_support/src/*.o and
the v1.12.14 runs compile none.

The framework package ships the same bootloader prebuilt, one ELF per flash
mode. Both envs are dio at 80m, so both take bootloader_dio_80m.elf.

This writes what lands at 0x0 on a first install, which is the exact class of
mistake recorded in this file's own comments from v1.0.0 and v1.0.1, so it is
verified rather than reasoned about. Converted with elf2image from
framework-arduinoespressif32-libs 5.5.0+sha.87912cd291 -- the version CI now
resolves -- the result is byte-identical to the bootloader in BOTH published
v1.12.13 full images:

  prebuilt        09c6a477ac9b33721e9ea455fda1e29dc5b2f35c85d0b858b693defcab6f19fb
  x4pro shipped   09c6a477ac9b33721e9ea455fda1e29dc5b2f35c85d0b858b693defcab6f19fb
  sticky shipped  09c6a477ac9b33721e9ea455fda1e29dc5b2f35c85d0b858b693defcab6f19fb

The step keeps a bootloader.bin that a build did produce, so if the IDF
compile ever comes back this becomes a no-op rather than an override.

host-tests/release asserts the ordering rather than the mechanism: whatever
supplies the file must supply it before the step that merges it. Watched it
fail with the step removed, naming both envs, and pass when restored.

Board card #155.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

chore: crossplay 1.12.14

Released by crossplay-autorelease after a green CI run on xteink.

docs: link the fork's own user guide from the front page

USER_GUIDE.md is titled "CrossPlay User Guide" and was adapted for this
fork, and nothing on the front page pointed at it. The only links to it
are from three docs a reader reaches after already knowing it exists.
Someone who has just flashed a device has nowhere to go for the controls,
the reader or the web server.

Its opening line also still named only the X4 Pro, a release after the
Sticky started shipping in the same images.

Docs: this is the docs fix. Triage: no card. Dream check: unchanged.

fix: six accuracy faults a cold reader found in the new README

A stranger read the rewritten front page with no context. Four of these
are mine, made in the rewrite; two were already there.

**The touch panel went missing, and it is what makes the shelf parse.**
The old README said "both ESP32-S3 with the same 800x480 panel and
capacitive touch" and the rewrite dropped it while compressing the device
section. Without it "Minesweeper: tap to dig, hold to flag" and "Connect
Four: seven columns, one tap each" read as metaphors for a button press,
and the reader is left believing seven columns are driven by two keys.
The lede now carries the panel, the touch and the two buttons.

**"It is the whole thing, not a video and not a mock-up" was too strong.**
site/README.md:218 has always said Connections fetches its board at
runtime and nothing is canned for it, so the daily grid does not work in
the browser. One of the nineteen games does not run in the demo the
section is pitching. It says so now, and says why.

**"CrossPlay ships no puzzle content of its own" is false as written.**
The original sentence was about Connections and the rewrite generalised
it across the whole section, two paragraphs under "D&Diagrams: 64 of
them" and "Trivia: 50,000 questions". Scoped back, and it now
distinguishes fetch-as-you-open from downloaded-once-onto-the-card.

**The wrong-chip warning named the hazard and hid the reassurance.** It
said flashing a C3 "is a cross-chip flash", which names the mistake
without naming the outcome, then followed with "the firmware protects
you", which covers only the S3-to-S3 case and reads as general comfort.
It now says what the mistake used to cost (a bricked device) and that
install.js reads the chip and stops with "Nothing was written" before
writing anything, which also answers the question the heading asked and
never did: how to tell an X4 Pro from an X4. You do not have to; the
installer does.

**"Developer Mode is off until you turn it on, and says so on the panel."**
What the panel says is that the device will not deep-sleep while it is
on, which is docs/install.md's version and the true one.

**The trademark list was incomplete, and a list is the wrong shape.**
Both the README and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES enumerated owners and neither
had grown with the shelf: the README omitted Yahtzee and Wavelength, the
notices additionally omitted Knucklebones, Sea Salt & Paper and Toy
Battle. Both now cover any shelf game carrying a published game's name,
which cannot go stale when the twentieth game lands. The specific
designer and publisher credits stay, because those are attributions
rather than a list.

Docs: THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md changed in the same commit. Triage: no card.
Dream check: unchanged; this is the same front page, told true.

test: bind the README's shelf counts to Shelf.cpp and LinkPlay.h

shelf_coverage.py already checked that every shelf item is NAMED in the
README and on the site. It did not check the totals beside them, and a
total is the easiest thing in the file to leave behind: add a twentieth
game and every name check still passes while the sentence goes on saying
nineteen. That is the failure this suite exists for, one level up.

Two counts are now derived rather than trusted: "19 games and 5 apps"
against the kGames and kApps tables, and "Nine of the games play over
PLAY NEARBY" against LinkPlay.h's GameId enum. Both accept a digit or a
number word, because the README uses one of each. If either sentence is
reworded out of existence the check says so rather than passing on a
regex that stopped matching.

Seen to fail before being trusted: with the README mutated to "18 games"
and "Eight of the games", the suite prints both gaps; restored, it is
green and `git diff` on the README is empty.

This exists because the same commit put "19 games and 5 apps" on the
front page, which is a fact about Shelf.cpp written out as a literal, and
the project has paid for that shape repeatedly.

Docs: none affected, the suite documents itself in its header. Triage: no
card. Dream check: unchanged.
